problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.   Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.   Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{2\cdot 1+6\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{2\cdot 1+6\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ 

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}\,x}{‖x‖\,‖{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x‖} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 0+6\cdot 6+(-2)\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{6}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{36}{\sqrt{44}\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{36}{2\sqrt{11}\cdot 6} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{11}}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{3\sqrt{11}}{11})≈{25.24}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
